status: initially blind independent whole FS1-FS3 audit; freeze with complete report and sources

checks.concern: Official signed integer domain and degree versus term count
checks.reconstruction: Fresh official(b) check: m=n_off+1, and FS statements are unconditional algebraic claims, not a classification of x,y. No preliminary proof used.

checks.concern: Prime p, Fueter t, multiplicity k and power q conflated
checks.reconstruction: p>=5 for FS1, p>7 for FS2/FS3, 1<=t<=p-2 and integer k>=2 are distinct exact ranges.

checks.concern: Inverse basis converts F into the wrong moment
checks.reconstruction: In direct indices F uses a and M_r uses a^(-r). In Theta_a's inverse basis the direct inverse index is c, so sum c*u_c is M_1.

checks.concern: Wrong exponent in transformation rule
checks.reconstruction: Multiplying direct indices by h gives F(sigma_h theta)=hF(theta), M_r(sigma_h theta)=h^(-r)M_r(theta).

checks.concern: Unproved annihilator or group-ring membership imported
checks.reconstruction: Coefficient at sigma_c^-1 of sigma_a vartheta is r_a(c)/p. Thus Theta_a=(a-sigma_a)vartheta and psi_t=(1+sigma_t-sigma_(t+1))vartheta are integral in the defined intersection I.

checks.concern: Positivity or complement may fail at endpoints
checks.reconstruction: The step c/p lies strictly between0 and1 and both t,t+1 are nonzero. Consecutive floors give nu in{0,1}; floors at p-c give complementary coefficients.

checks.concern: Norm membership or weight requires an unused basis theorem
checks.reconstruction: psi+jpsi=N proves N in I and augmentation(p-1)/2. All sums and translates used preserve I, positivity and augmentation directly.

checks.concern: Moment zero confused with a converse test
checks.reconstruction: Residue/inverse sums give F(N)=M_1(N)=0. If M_1(theta) is nonzero, a fixed translate forces h^(-1)=1. No converse is claimed.

checks.concern: Illegitimate division by p or denominator6
checks.reconstruction: Expand exact sum(ac-pu_c)^2=sum c^2 modulo p^2, use integer S2/p, then reduce. At p>=5 all remaining divisors are units.

checks.concern: Derived square sum gives action functional instead
checks.reconstruction: The inverse-index coefficient is u_c; direct inverse of its index is c. Hence the sum is exactly M_1(Theta_a)=(a-a^-1)/12.

checks.concern: Wrong Bernoulli sign or p5 endpoint
checks.reconstruction: The exact fourth-power sum divided by p has reduction-1/30. Denominator30 is used only at p>=7, never p5.

checks.concern: Expansion term or cubic index omitted
checks.reconstruction: All second-and-higher p terms vanish modulo p^2; dividing gives4a^3 sum c^3u_c=(a^4-1)(-1/30), hence the displayed M_3 formula.

checks.concern: Subtracting consecutive a gives wrong numerator
checks.reconstruction: Subtraction gives Q(t)/(12t(t+1)) and -(1+t^-3-(t+1)^-3)/120 with distinct p>=5/p>=7 thresholds.

checks.concern: Only a Fourier test, not exact group-ring stabilizer
checks.reconstruction: Nonzero M_1 and the exact group action force the stabilizer itself to be{1}.

checks.concern: Q(t)=0 might give t=1
checks.reconstruction: At p>=5, Q(1)=3 is nonzero. Thus Q(t)=0 implies actual order3, whence3 divides p-1 and p>=7.

checks.concern: A vanishing moment does not prove invariance
checks.reconstruction: The integer sum c+r_t(c)+r_(t^2)(c)-p cycles under c->r_t(c). This is exactly the coefficient action of sigma_t on the inverse basis.

checks.concern: Larger stabilizer not excluded
checks.reconstruction: M_3=-1/40 is nonzero at the admissible exceptional primes; invariance forces h^3=1. Three roots already lie in the stabilizer, exhausting it.

checks.concern: M_1 zero silently identified with F zero
checks.reconstruction: F=0 follows separately from sigma_t invariance, F(sigma_t psi)=tF(psi), and t!=1. M_1=0 follows from its own formula.

checks.concern: p3 or p5 invalidates exceptional criterion
checks.reconstruction: p5 has no order3 subgroup and never needs M_3. At p3,t1 the literal psi=sigma2 is free although Q(1)=0, so exclusion is necessary. A hand p7,t2 support check confirms order3.

checks.concern: Fermat quotient identity requires a theorem not checked
checks.reconstruction: Expand product(ac-pu_c), cancel the unit factorial and divide an integer congruence by p. This yields sum u_c/c=(a^p-a)/p modulo p without an external Voronoi import.

checks.concern: Function reduction changes polynomial coefficients
checks.reconstruction: ((X+1)^p-X^p-1)/p is integral with degree p-1, zeros0,-1, and coefficients(-1)^(j-1)/j at p-j for j1..5 before any function reduction.

checks.concern: Nonconstancy on all indices leaves only zero-moment witnesses
checks.reconstruction: The argument explicitly deletes0,-1 and all Q-roots, so both chosen inverse moments are nonzero. It proves nonconstancy on that domain itself.

checks.concern: Deleted points are not roots of P
checks.reconstruction: The outer Q handles Q-roots; f and X(X+1) vanish at0,-1; the assumed constant identity handles every other point.

checks.concern: Pointwise zero used as polynomial zero
checks.reconstruction: Only divisibility by the product of the p distinct linear factors X^p-X is inferred, with quotient degree3. No polynomial identity P=0 is asserted.

checks.concern: Low/high degrees overlap or7/10 vanishes
checks.reconstruction: For p>7, degree p-1 is between the high part>=p and low part<=4. Q^2 times the leading coefficients gives7/10, and the C term has degree4. This is nonzero for every written p.

checks.concern: Division by a zero action moment
checks.reconstruction: If either chosen F value is zero, double that Fueter element. Its inverse moment remains nonzero because p is odd. Both F values cannot vanish when the products differ.

checks.concern: A negative residue creates a negative coefficient
checks.reconstruction: sigma_(-f(s)) is a positive coefficient permutation. The two nonzero indices cancel F while M_1=(u(s)-u(t))/(f(s)f(t)) stays nonzero.

checks.concern: Kernel, weight or relative identity lost in construction
checks.reconstruction: Both cases give theta in I_f, nonnegative coefficients, augmentation p-1, complement2N and trivial stabilizer by the direct moment test.

checks.concern: Rediscovery presented as a new existence theorem
checks.reconstruction: Fresh primary Lemma2.7 and Appendix5.2 check confirms the same one-element/two-moment selection route. Candidate attributes overlap and uses its own p>7 proof, not an imported appendix or small-prime extension.

checks.concern: Only one zero may exist
checks.reconstruction: Complement2N gives a0/2 pair unless theta=N, which its moment excludes. A single zero at v forces theta=N-sigma_v+sigma_-v and F=-2v, contradicting F=0.

checks.concern: Wrong ratio or opposite-zero case
checks.reconstruction: For distinct zeros v,w, complement2N excludes v=-w. Taking h=v/w gives h!=1,-1 and the shifted direct coefficient at v equal to n_w=0.

checks.concern: No exact extremum or moment cancellation
checks.reconstruction: Common zero and gamma+jgamma=4N give extrema0,4. M_1(gamma)=(1+h^-1)M_1(theta) is nonzero; kernel membership and positivity are preserved.

checks.concern: Family members have unequal weights or negative entries
checks.reconstruction: k-l>=1 and k-2>=0 ensure positivity. All A_l and B have augmentation k(p-1), and their complements are2kN.

checks.concern: Reduced moment can vanish when p divides a scalar
checks.reconstruction: Cancel the nonzero integer k-l in the torsion-free Z-module Z[G], not in F_p. Freeness survives every integer k>=2 even when the reduced moment is zero.

checks.concern: Adding a norm vector changes the stabilizer
checks.reconstruction: The added vector is G-invariant, so B has exactly gamma's stabilizer.

checks.concern: Pairwise nonconjugacy not established
checks.reconstruction: Each A_l has exact minimum l and maximum2k-l. B has minimum k-2, leaving only A_(k-2) as a possible conjugate.

checks.concern: Strict norm inequality disappears after adding N
checks.reconstruction: ||gamma||^2=4||theta||^2-||theta-sigma_h theta||^2 is strict by freeness and h!=1. Equal augmentations make the common norm addition's cross terms equal, preserving strictness.

checks.concern: Same Fourier value may hide distinct integer vectors
checks.reconstruction: The kernel polynomial's degree<=p-1 and constant0 force it to vanish after divisibility by Phi_p. Equivariance then proves within-orbit freeness and cross-orbit disjointness exactly.

checks.concern: Higher weight substituted into a weight-p-1 source estimate
checks.reconstruction: Actual original definitions/Lemma3/application require augmentation p-1. FS3 has k times that weight. The candidate retains new interpolation, integrality, all-conjugate, nonzero-delta and size tasks rather than claiming their discharge.

checks.concern: k1 or p7 inferred from a successful larger-domain argument
checks.reconstruction: gamma-N has coefficient-1 at the common zero, and7/10 vanishes at p7. Neither endpoint extension, nonexistence or full Diophantine conclusion is asserted.

checks.concern: Relative weight confused with augmentation or absolute weight
checks.reconstruction: Later relative weight2 is augmentation p-1; FS3 relative weight is2k. For positive vectors absolute coefficient sum equals augmentation. No factor is dropped when comparing source requirements.

checks.concern: Claimed |beta|=y^k has wrong exponent
checks.reconstruction: Under the explicitly conditional beta^p equation and complement2kN, |beta|^(2p)=G_p(x)^(2k)=y^(2kp), hence |beta|=y^k for y>0. No beta existence is inferred.

checks.concern: Original Fourier injectivity copied into later normalized map
checks.reconstruction: Opposite-index reciprocal pairs have a common sum and yield a nonzero kernel difference. FS3 uses only faithful Fourier E and does not transfer its disjoint lists to that map.

checks.concern: k divisible by p treated only by a finite sample
checks.reconstruction: The exact integer cancellation argument covers every k>=2 and every nonzero factor k-l; no sample, divisibility exception or upper bound on k is needed.

checks.concern: Fermat quotient depends on an integer lift
checks.reconstruction: Theta_a uses the stated positive lift, while f(t) is the exact consecutive-difference integer polynomial reduced mod p. Its polynomial use never replaces a standalone Fermat quotient by a lift-invariant function.

checks.concern: The extra orbit degenerates at the smallest k
checks.reconstruction: At k2, B=gamma and A_(k-2)=2theta; their zero minima agree but the strict integer norm inequality separates them. The remaining A1 has minimum1.

checks.concern: Unverified original counting or appendix proof is a hidden premise
checks.reconstruction: Neither is used to prove FS. The current own nonconstancy proof covers the required nonexceptional domain and zero F cases. Full external Diophantine proof is neither accepted nor refuted.

checks.reconstruction: C/PG/CF1/MS accepted bodies and narrow StrongFC status were read. Their hypotheses/ranges remain context, not extra exclusions or universal class-number premises.
